prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an upward-tilted indoor scene where a windowed wall recedes diagonally from roughly 1.5 m on the left to over 4 m in the dark upper-right corner and ceiling (~3–4 m above). A man's head and upper shoulders appear in the lower center of all five frames at roughly 1.2–1.8 m from the camera wearer, while a bright white foreground silhouette enters on the lower left in frames 3–5 within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m away and ~1 m in front of and to the left of the man), alongside a small raised hand silhouette to the man's right in frame 4. Across the sequence, the man dips lower in frame 2, turns into right profile in frames 3–4 while staying at a similar depth, and appears slightly larger and nearer (~1.2 m) facing the camera wearer in frame 5 as the left foreground intrusion recedes and re-enters as a hand. The depth map makes the continuous recession of the wall and the sharp depth separation between the near-field occlusion and the mid-ground man much clearer than the backlit RGB image, where both appear as dark shapes against the bright sky. However, the map is unreliable on the window glass—rendering the outdoor sky at the same depth as the window frames—and exhibits a noticeable global brightness drop in frame 3 when the very close left object enters the frame.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates two `person` instances along the bottom frame boundary against an unsegmented black background: the central man (pink mask) at ~1.2–1.8 m in front of the camera wearer across all five frames, and a second `person` instance (brown mask) entering on the lower left in frames 3–5 within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m from the camera wearer and ~1 m left of the central man). Both individuals are heavily truncated by the image borders, with the central man cropped below the shoulders and the left instance only partially visible as a fuzzy clothed shoulder/arm in frames 3–4 and a bare hand in frame 5. Over the five frames, the central mask drops lower in frame 2, shifts slightly right during frames 3–4 while the left person mask advances and retreats at the left edge, and expands in frame 5 as the man faces the camera wearer from slightly closer. These instance masks clearly delineate the boundary of the close left intruder and the backlit man despite glare from the windows in the RGB strip. However, the map provides no head orientation or gaze information, misses all room structure (windows, walls, overhead light) as well as the raised hand visible to the right of the man in frame 4, and inconsistently labels the close hand in frame 5 as a separate person without body context.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse yellow head and upper-neck keypoints on a black background only for the central man (~1.2–1.8 m away) in frames 2 and 5, leaving frames 1, 3, and 4 completely blank and detecting no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In frame 2, a short cluster of facial landmarks near the bottom center indicates the man's head is facing toward the camera wearer, and in frame 5, facial keypoints connected to a vertical neck/upper-torso segment show him tilted slightly back and looking toward the camera wearer while his torso is cut off below the frame. Using the RGB strip for context, the man actually faces the camera wearer in frames 1–2, turns his head to his left (viewer's right) into profile during frames 3–4 while a hand rises near the lower right edge, and turns back toward the camera wearer in frame 5 while another person's arm or hand enters within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) on the lower left. Where detected, the facial landmarks help pinpoint eye and nose positions on the heavily backlit face that is dark in the RGB frames. Nevertheless, the pose map is largely unreliable across the sequence because severe lower-border cropping of the bodies causes complete detection failures in frames 1, 3, and 4, and it misses both the close left person/hand and the raised right hand entirely.
